name: Bayraktar TB2
operator: Turkey and many export customers worldwide
overview_md:
The Bayraktar TB2 is Turkey's combat-proven armed drone and the aircraft that, more than any other, demonstrated how a cheap medium-altitude UAV could reshape modern warfare. Built by Baykar, it is far smaller and less expensive than a Reaper or Wing Loong, yet armed with lightweight precision MAM-series munitions it has proved devastating against armour, air defences and artillery in a string of recent conflicts.

The TB2's combat record is its calling card: it was decisive in the 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh war, struck Russian forces in the opening phase of the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, and saw heavy use in Libya and Syria. A turboprop-powered aircraft with around 27 hours of endurance and four hardpoints, it is controlled by line-of-sight and satellite links and has been exported to dozens of countries, becoming a symbol of the democratisation of precision airpower.

For an analyst, the TB2 is included here as the benchmark for the "cheap mass" school of drone warfare, against which the larger MQ-9 and Wing Loong are judged. Its Indo-Pacific footprint is smaller than in Europe and the Middle East, but its influence is global: it proved that affordable, exportable armed drones can blunt conventional forces — a lesson now shaping how regional militaries from South to Southeast Asia think about both fielding and defeating unmanned strike.

armament_json.name: MAM-L / MAM-C
armament_json.notes: Smart micro-munitions; devastating vs armour and air defence

variants_json.name: TB2S / Akıncı (heavier sibling)
variants_json.key_changes: Satellite-control TB2 and the larger Akıncı UCAV

combat_history.event: TB2s destroyed large numbers of Armenian tanks, vehicles and air-defence systems, helping decide the war.
combat_history.significance: Showcased how cheap drones could defeat conventional ground forces.

combat_history.event: TB2s struck advancing Russian columns in the opening weeks of the invasion of Ukraine.
combat_history.significance: Cemented the TB2's reputation and inspired a wave of drone procurement.

modernization.description: Beyond-line-of-sight TB2S and the much larger, more capable Akıncı UCAV.
modernization.impact: Extends Baykar's reach into higher-end unmanned strike.

vulnerabilities.description: Slow, low-flying and lightly built; highly vulnerable once an enemy fields functional air defence.
vulnerabilities.context: TB2 losses rose sharply once Russia restored its air-defence net in Ukraine.
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Best against degraded or absent air defence.

vulnerabilities.description: Small munitions limit it to soft and lightly-armoured targets.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Cheap, persistent armed ISR against ground forces and air defences in permissive or degraded-air-defence environments.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Operated by a wide range of national militaries; networked into local C2.
operational_patterns.readiness_notes: Mature and exported to dozens of countries.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The Reaper has far greater endurance, payload and sensors; the TB2 wins decisively on cost and availability.
The Wing Loong is larger and heavier-armed; the TB2 is cheaper and more combat-celebrated.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: The armed-drone export market's price tiers.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The Shahed is a one-way attack drone; the TB2 is a reusable armed ISR platform.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: Reusable drones vs one-way attack drones.

doctrine.role: Low-cost combat-proven armed ISR drone for precision strike against ground forces and air defences.
doctrine.employment: Persistent surveillance then precision micro-munition strikes, most effective where enemy air defence is weak or degraded.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Affordable, exportable precision airpower — cheap mass over high-end capability.
doctrine.threat_context: The benchmark for the 'cheap drone' revolution; globally influential even where its Indo-Pacific footprint is modest.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against the MQ-9 and Wing Loong (capability) and the Shahed (reusable vs one-way).
